topic: Binary Counting and the Towers of Hanoi: The Hidden Logic
target_audience: High school students interested in computer science and discrete mathematics

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Language of Bits
lecture_lines: Binary digits represent powers of two.
animations: Represent decimal 13 as powers of two.

sections.title: The Towers of Hanoi: Rules of the Game
lecture_lines: Three rods hold disks of different sizes.
Rule: Move one disk at a time.
Rule: No larger disk on a smaller one.
animations: Animate discs stacked on rods using #FF4500.
Show illegal move restriction (large on small) in #FF0000.

sections.title: The Binary Connection
lecture_lines: Disk moves mirror binary counting patterns.
Binary steps determine which disk moves.
animations: Move disk 2 while binary counts up.
Show binary counting table next to rods.
Flash the binary number when a disk moves.

sections.title: Application and Complexity
lecture_lines: Minimum moves equal two to the n minus one.
Complexity grows exponentially with more disks.
This puzzle demonstrates recursive algorithmic logic.
animations: Label the curve with growth rate.

sections.title: Conclusion and Summary
lecture_lines: Binary counting defines the Hanoi solution.
Recursive problems often share this structure.
Simple binary logic hides deep complexity.
animations: Summarize Binary and Hanoi relation in #FFFFFF.
Fade in "Binary logic dictates complexity" text.
